newsitem.title: UK: Italy's Prodi says "more confident" of joining EMU.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi says "more confident" of joining EMU.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday he was more confident that Italy would be among the first wave of nations to enter a single European currency.

Asked if he was still confident would that Italy would be on the starting line for European Economic and Monetary Union, Prodi said in an interview to be broadcast on CCN: "I am not still confident, I am more confident."
Prodi said he knew that German public opinion was against Italy entering EMU. "I don't want to be judged by internal political problems. I want to be judged by objective rules," he said.
He said scepticism about Italy's ability to meet the Maastricht criteria and join EMU in the first wave was decreasing.
Prodi said if Italy met the necessary targets, no-one could stop them from entering. "But if I don't meet the criteria, I will stay out."

He said one of the main benefits of making the first round would be the reduction in long-term interest rates that would result. Interest payments currently constitute the largest burden on the Italian budget.
With interest rates lower on a sustainable basis, Prodi said that would help Italy to meet any stability pact requirements concerning the size of public debt.
